findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the handwashing sink in the bar area did not have paper towels. CORRECTED: PIC supplied the handwashing sink with paper towels during the inspection. Ensure that each handwashing sink is provided everything a person needs to wash their hands: hot water, soap, paper towels, and a trash can.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw shell eggs stored above ready-to-eat food in the first walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: PIC moved the eggs to separate shelf where it is stored away from RTE foods and not above RTE foods. Ensure that raw eggs are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Sanitizer bucket near the front handwashing sink was observed with no measurable Chlorine sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED: An employee added a capful of bleach and the bucket tested at 150 ppm (Cl) afterwards. The PIC was reminded that sanitizer solutions must be checked on a regular basis. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration (Cl = 50-150ppm).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: A spray bottle of clear liquid was observed on the hibachi station cart without a label. CORRECTED: Per PIC, this spray bottle contains degreaser. Ensure all working containers of chemicals are labeled to indicate their contents using common names (in this case, “degreaser”).
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Employee vitamins and supplements were observed stored intermixed with items for service in the sushi station. CORRECTED: PIC moved items to separate storage away from items for service, into the areas designated for employee use.
findings.citation_text: 7-208.11(B) Storage. First aid supplies that are in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for the EMPLOYEES' use shall be: (B) Stored in a kit or a container that is located to prevent the contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed multiple containers of cooked rice that were cooling inside of sealed plastic containers. The rice had only been cooling for about 30 minutes. CORRECTED: PIC was educated that containers must be uncovered during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Inspectors and PIC also discussed using shallower pans (like baking trays) to cool the rice, as they cool faster than deep trays. During the inspection the covers were removed. Ensure that food is always cooled using the proper procedure.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(B) Cooling Methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers in which FOOD is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the EQUIPMENT to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed fish with a label stating that it must be removed from the reduced oxygen environment before thawing was thawing within the package in the sushi station. CORRECTED: The PIC was educated and employees removed the fish from the packaging. Ensure that reduced oxygen packaged fish is always removed from the package before thawing.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Facility does not have a probe thermometer readily accessible. Ensure that at least one probe thermometer is available within the facility for use monitoring internal food temperatures. Inspector will Follow Up to confirm a probe thermometer is available.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Adhesive fly strips were observed placed above prep counters throughout the kitchen as a preventative measure. Inspectors and PIC discussed better placement of the strips. Ensure that fly strips and other insect control devices are placed where they would not potentially contaminate foods or food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed single-service and single-use articles stored with their food-contact surfaces unprotected. CORRECTED: PIC inverted the to-go containers and bowls so that their food-contact surfaces were not upright and exposed to contamination form falling debris, and PIC moved additional plates to a lower shelf so they were protected from above. Ensure all single-service and single-use articles are protected from contamination by necessary means.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the employee bathroom, which is used by all genders, does not have a covered trash can. Discussed with PIC that any bathroom that can be used by women needs to have a covered receptacle to dispose of sanitary napkins, for both hygiene reasons and to protect the establishment’s plumbing.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The employee restroom is in need of repairs:
(i) the wall behind the sink is deteriorating so that it is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Repair wall so it is smooth and easily cleanable. Consider adding a Nudo board panel to resurface damaged walls.
(ii) chemical storage shelving is made of unsealed particleboard and plywood. Paint or otherwise seal shelving so it is smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee rinse their gloved hands in the dump sink. When the action was observed the employee was instructed to remove gloves, wash hands in the hand washing sink, and put on a new pair of gloves. The PIC will be further educating employees about proper glove use and hand washing. Ensure that hands are always properly washed in hand washing sink to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed several dented cans on the storage rack. During the inspection the dented cans were removed from service. Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect the integrity of the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw, cracked shell eggs stored on the top shelf of the silver refrigerator on the cookline over various ready-to-eat vegetables. During the inspection the eggs were moved onto the bottom shelf. Ensure that raw eggs are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross contamination.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the ice machine baffles have an accumulation of debris. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris and other soil residues. An inspector will follow-up on 2/2/2026 to ensure that the ice machine baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed fish with a label stating that it must be removed from the reduced oxygen environment before thawing was thawing within the package in the front walk-in cooler and sushi station. The PIC was educated and employees removed the fish from the packaging. Ensure that reduced oxygen packaged fish is always removed from the package before thawing.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed several unpackaged white powders on the cookline are not labeled. The PIC was educated that any easily mistaken foods removed from the original container must be labeled with the common name of the food. Ensure that the unpackaged white powders are properly labeled by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the reach-in freezer on the cookline has a significant buildup of frost. Ensure that the freezer is defrosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the following cooler interior fans have an accumulation of dust: (1) The single door cooler by the kitchen entrance (THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION ); (2) The single door cooler by the triple sink; (3) The single door cooler by the dish machine; and (4) The back walk-in cooler. Ensure that the fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the floor between the soda machine and dump sink in the server station has an accumulation of soda spills and other debris. Ensure that the floor is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed employees on the cookline were not washing hands between removing gloves and putting on new ones. The employees on the cookline were educated that hands must be washed before donning gloves to initiate tasks that involve working with food. The PIC will be continuing to educated employees about the proper procedure. Ensure that employees always wash hands when switching gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the sushi hand washing sink was blocked with a container of vegetables. The employees at the sushi station were educated that the hand washing sink must always be accessible. During the inspection the container was removed from across the hand washing sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are always maintained accessible at all times for employee use.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed plastic containers holding various sauces and seasonings on the cookline were soiled with debris. The PIC discarded the soiled plastic containers and replaced them with new containers during the inspection. They were reminded that the plastic containers must be replaced on a regular basis to avoid soil accumulation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed glass cleaner re-packaged from the original container into spray bottles were not labeled. During the inspection the glass cleaner at the sushi station and by the mop sink were labeled with the common name. Ensure that toxic materials taken from bulk supply are always clearly labeled with the common name of the material.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Observed there are not ambient air thermometers inside of the coolers at the sushi station and the main kitchen. There are thermometers inside the walk-in coolers. The ambient air thermometers must be placed at the warmest part of the cooler (i.e., next to the door). Ensure that every cooler has an ambient air thermometer by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed that the bar hand washing sink is not sealed to the wall. Ensure that the hand sink is sealed to the wall (ex. caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The accumulated debris behind the nozzles of the server soda machine. 

(2) The dust on the fans of the single door cooler by the kitchen entrance. 

(3) The dust, drink spills, and other debris inside of the clear door cooler under the back counter at the bar. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the cove base has fallen off the wall to the right of the kitchen back door and on the corner to the left of the front walk-in cooler. Ensure the cove base is repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the mop head stored on the mop sink basin. The PIC and employees were educated that mops must be stored in a position that allows the head to air-dry. The mop was hung on the rack during the inspection. Ensure that mop heads are always stored to facilitate air-drying.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the ceiling in the alcohol storage room (also stores single-use articles and food contact surfaces) at the back of the kitchen is damaged in the back right corner. Ensure that the ceiling is repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the left sink at the sushi station that is used for hand washing did not have hand washing signage. The right sink that is used for dumping was labeled with hand washing signage. The signage was removed from the designated dump sink and the PIC was given new hand washing signage for the designed hand washing sink. Ensure that signage that notifies employees to wash hands before returning to work is available at every hand washing sink.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the dump sink (to the left of the reach-in freezer). Stored behind the faucets the cutting board can be contaminated by water splashes, food residue, and other debris dumped into the sink. The cutting board was moved to a different location for storage during the inspection Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the dish machine was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. The employee working the dish machine drained the water and the dish machine tested at 100 ppm (Cl) afterwards. The PIC stated that the dish machine repair company suggested draining the water every two hours at the last visit. The inspector reminded that PIC that the dish machine must be tested regularly to make sure that it is functioning correctly (test strips are stored on top of the dish machine). Ensure that the dish machine is always properly sanitizing.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the fried rice in the warmer across from the dish machine had an internal temperature of about 125F. The PIC stated that the rice was put inside the warmer at 11 am when the facility opened. During the inspection the temperature of the warmer was turned up and the rice had an internal temperature of 178F when the inspector re-checked. A time-as-control policy was implemented for the rice. The facility closes at 2:30 pm and any leftover rice will be discarded at this time. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods are maintained at 135F or higher.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed several pans of cooked rice in the back walk-in cooler stacked together that did not all have date marking. Each item must be individually labeled in case the pans are separated. Ensure that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the seven day maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed the large containers holding various un-packaged white powders were not properly labeled. The containers did not have labels that matched the food inside (ex. flour was in the container labeled corn starch). The PIC stated they will be removing the old labels and creating new labels that match. Ensure that all easily mistaken foods not in the original container are properly labeled with the common name.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Observed the following foods stored in a position that presents the risk of contamination:

(1) Uncovered fried tempura on the sushi prep line; the lid was put onto the container during the inspection. 

(2) Uncovered cut vegetables in the walk-in cooler; saran wrap was put on to cover the containers during the inspection. 

(3) A hammer stored on top of foods in the dry storage area; the hammer was moved into the personal storage bin.

All staff members were observed practicing improper handwashing technique and frequency. Hands were washed in non-handwashing sinks, without using proper barriers, for durations too short to be effective, and without proper hand soap usage. Hands were not washing following potentially contaminating actions and activities such as touching head/hair, putting hands in pockets, using personal phones and other devices, blowing/wiping noses, and others. 

Inspector is present due to the concern of a foodborne illness being contracted as this establishment. Viruses and other pathogens are easily spread by touch from the contaminated hands of staff. To prevent additional illness from occurring, the facility MUST enforce proper hand washing procedure and frequency as follows:

- Hands must be washed EVERY TIME contamination has occurred. Discuss with staff the need to be aware of what they are touching, if the surfaces they touch are cleaned and sanitized, and if not, that hands are immediately washed. Personal devices, insides of clothing, and areas of the body are not cleaned and sanitized surfaces and once touched ALWAYS requires that staff wash hands afterward. Wiping noses is an EXTREMELY hazardous behavior and should NEVER occur in the kitchen and must ALWAYS be followed up with proper hand washing.

- Hands must be washed with active scrubbing for a minimum of 20 seconds.
- Hand soap must be used every time hands are washed.
- Hands may only be washed in designated hand washing sinks, never a triple sink, dump sink, disk sink or utility sink. 
- A barrier such as a paper towel must be used to turn off the faucet. If staff fails to use a barrier to turn off the faucet, hands must be immediately rewashed.

** Gloves are NOT an alternative to proper hand washing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
The severity of violations observed during the investigation indicates a complete failure to protect food and food-contact surfaces from contamination. The following observations were made:
- All staff members were observed handling personal phones in the kitchen, at the sushi station, in the server stations, at the bar, and at the front counter. 
- Multiple staff members were observed touching body parts or clothing and continuing to work with food and/or food-contact surfaces.
- Exiting the facility and returning without proper hand washing.
- Blowing/wiping noses and faces with facility paper towels and not subsequent hand washing.
- Picking at skin/sores on the hands before working with clean food-contact surfaces.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
A shallow metal container of shelled eggs was stored on the top shelf of the upright cooler along the west wall of the kitchen. Several foods including raw beef and raw scallops were stored directly below this container of eggs. A recent complaint for possible foodborne illness indicated that one affected individual consumed scallops prior to the onset of symptoms. Storage order of raw animal products contributes to cross-contamination and is a potential source of illness. The container did not have a lid or any other covering to prevent contamination from the eggs to items beneath them. Stored raw foods must be stored in a manner, based on cooking temperatures, which prevents cross-contamination. Fish and pork must be cooked to a lower temperature of 145 degrees F for 15 seconds and thus should be stored above all other raw animal products but below ANY ready-to-eat foods. Beef must be cooked to 155 degrees F for 15 seconds and should be stored below fish and pork but above poultry. Poultry (including eggs) must be stored below other food items to prevent cross-contamination because it requires the highest cooking temperature of 165 degrees F. Ensure that staff are aware of proper storage order and the reason for separation and that foods are all separated in a manner that prevents contamination during storage. Should the facility require handouts or further education regarding proper storage order, reach out to Sangamon County Department of Public Health (SCDPH) immediately.

Operator immediately removed the container of shelled eggs and placed it on the bottom shelf next to the carboard container of other shelled eggs already located on the bottom shelf. Corrected on site. No follow-up required.

Inspector observed countertops which food is prepared on being wiped down with water that had no sanitizer present. An operator immediately added two capfuls of bleach to the water with a Cl concentration of 100 ppm and the counter was wiped down properly. Corrected on site. 

The dish machine was observed to be operating with a bleach concentration greater than 200 ppm chlorine. No label is present on the machine to indicate operating parameters for bleach concentration. The machine is serviced by GFS. Contact GFS to ensure that proper bleach concentrations are being used in the dish machine. 

Two sanitizer buckets in the facility were observed to have concentrations of sanitizer too low to measure using SCDPH test strips. Concentrations high enough to register on facility test strips were obtained by soaking and stirring the test strips in the water. Ensure that test strips are used properly and that sanitizer meets concentration requirements. 

4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed cleaned/sanitized bowls in a soiled container and with a piece of green onion sitting on top of the bowls. Dishes must be protected from contamination and must be cleaned/sanitized properly when contamination occurs. 

The blade of the can opener was observed to be soiled with old, dry food. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized often. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Date marking was inconsistent throughout the facility. The upright cooler to the right of the triple sink was observed to have no date marking at all. All other coolers had a mix of date marked items and items missing date marking. Ensure that date marking is occurring throughout the facility on all items requiring date marking. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wet wiping cloths were observed sitting on counters throughout the facility and in buckets with too low a concentration of sanitizer to remain sanitary. Wiping cloths, when not in use, must be stored in sanitizer solution. Ensure that wiping cloths are ONLY stored in sanitizing solution between uses. This is a repeat violation. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The facility is in need of deep cleaning throughout. Most pieces of equipment are heavily soiled in all hard-to-reach areas. Easily reached areas appear to be cleaned regularly but details are frequently missed allowing residue and debris to accumulate throughout the facility. Ensure that all equipment is cleaned often enough to prevent accumulation of residue and debris. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Physical facilities appear clean ONLY is easy to clean places. Underneath all equipment and most corners of the kitchen and sushi bar there are large amounts of debris on the floor and particularly in corners. Deep cleaning must occur in underneath ALL equipment by the next routine inspection and must remain clean. Cleaning must occur at a frequency that precludes the accumulation of residue and debris. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
All sinks in the kitchen have damaged/missing/deteriorating caulk. Ensure that all sinks are caulked to create a smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surface. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
During the prior inspection when this follow-up was issued, person-in-charge was instructed to clean the side portions of the hibachi grill between the drop-in grill itself and the countertop. Modest cleaning was performed as there was still residue in these areas, but they were much less soiled than previously, and the possibility exists that the remaining debris/residue was from food service over the past 10-days. However, one grill still had the same amount of debris and residue in this area and had not been cleaned. As an area of potential concern for pests following a complaint, these are significant harborage conditions that must not exist in the facility. Ensure that the areas discussed in the prior inspection are ALL clean prior to the follow-up date issued for 11/28/2022 to prevent mice and other pests from worsening in the facility. Inspector observed no active pests at this time.  

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
During the inspection of the hibachi grills resulting from a pest complaint, inspector observed that two of the grills had drips on them. Upon investigation of the drips, the lights and hood above the grills was observed to be heavily soiled with blackened grease and other residue. This residue has accumulated to the point of dripping which poses a potential contamination hazard. Discussion with person-in-charge indicated that the facility is aware and cleans the grills before each service but neglects the hoods and possibility of contamination should these residues drip onto food during preparation underneath the hoods/light fixtures. Facility advised inspector that cleaning of these hoods is performed in-house. Clean the hoods and light fixtures to remove all residue from them. If sufficient cleaning cannot be performed in-house, have a third-party service perform routine cleaning. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent such residues from accumulating. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector did not observe any active pests/nest or other indication of cockroaches in the facility. Operator states that he has not seen any cockroaches in the establishment. Although no pests were observed, there were some concerning harborage conditions at each hibachi grill. Each grill, along both sides from the front to back, is heavily soiled in the area underneath the baffling of the grill. These areas have a large amount of food debris and grease which has begun to pile up. This is a harborage condition for pests and must be eliminated immediately. Inspector checked each of these areas and no insects were observed. Underneath the triple sink and dish machine of the facility is a large amount of soil along with underneath the grill and fryer in the kitchen. These are also harborage conditions for pests. Pest prevention is reliant on good cleaning practices. Ensure that moving forward, cleaning of these concerning areas is performed routinely. A follow-up is being issued for 10-days. At that time, these areas must be clean to sight and touch. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; 

Hand sink in the prep area of kitchen, next to mop sink, did not have paper towels in dispenser. A roll of packaged paper towels was sat on top of dispenser. Discussed with PIC, ensure staff are properly re-stocking soap and towels as they are emptied so the next person can properly wash hands. COS- towels were opened and placed in dispensers.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

Observed a bottle of lemon juice in the handsink upon entry to the kitchen. Also observed a steel wool in the sushi bar handsink. Discussed with PIC- see that staff do not put items in the handsink or use the handwashing sink for any other purposes besides handwashing. COS- PIC removed the items from the handsink. 

See that staff are educated on the uses/non-uses of the handsink in the facility.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

In the hibachi prep cooler, observed prepped containers of sliced vegetables with store-bought containers of the same veggie placed within the prepped containers. Discussed with PIC. See that staff are not placing containers of any kind in prepped food items as the bottom of the container may be a source of cross contamination for the food. COS- PIC removed the containers and advised kitchen staff on where to store the unopened containers.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Racks in walk-in cooler, storing containers of rice and noodles, observed to have an accumulation of debris/mold. See that the racks are washed, rinsed, and sanitized by follow up date.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The handwashing sink next to the dish machine, next to the mop sink, and the prep sink next to the fryer station appear to be detaching from the wall, creating a gap behind. See that the sinks are re-secured to the wall and caulking is replaced to render it smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.110: Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

Observed a staff cell phone stored on the side edge of the hibachi prep cooler in kitchen. Discussed with PIC and staff present in the prep area. See that cell phones are used in designated spaces only, during breaks. Do not store cell phones in/on any prep surfaces or equipment in facility. Do not use cell phones in the kitchen.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Observed an employee use sanitizer rag to sanitize work station and proceed to use same gloves to engage in food preparation. Discussed with PIC. See general comments regarding training needed for staff.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

Observed food debris in the hand sink by the dish machine. Ensure staff are not using hand sink for any purposes other than handwashing. Food debris should be disposed of in a designated sink for dumping and/or a trash can. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Several new employees lack employee health reporting agreements signed and on file. Discussed with PICs. Compile employee health paperwork by next routine inspection

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

Trays of individually prepared side salads observed stacked on top of each other in the glass cooler by dish machine. Discussed contamination concern with PIC. Bottom of trays sat directly on top of salads with no barrier, exposing salads to potential contamination at bottom of tray. 
COS- staff will cover salad trays with plastic wrap to prevent bottom of trays from being in direct contact with food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several hibachi carts are observed stored in back room soiled with crumbs and food debris from last night’s dinner service. Discussed with PIC. Carts must be washed, rinsed, and sanitized properly right after service before storing. COS- PIC and staff pulled carts for cleaning.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less.

Hibachi carts observed stored in back storage room. On one cart, a container of raw shell eggs and a container of butter stored on cart. Eggs and butter discarded by PIC at time of inspection. Ensure hibachi staff either discard foods leftover from dinner service or place into cold holding. TCS foods should not be left out overnight.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. 

Several coolers in establishment lack a thermometer within the unit to measure ambient air temperature. Some include: sushi display and prep coolers, Coca Cola coolers in server and cooking stations, protein cooler in kitchen, and prep cooler at the wok station. Discussed with PIC. Although these units have digital monitors, thermometers should be within to most accurately measure temperature. Will follow up.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14:  (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. 

Wet wiping cloths stored on hibachi cart in back stock area of kitchen. All wet cloths should be in an appropriate sanitizer solution. No wet wiping cloths out in ambient air. Ensure hibachi staff do not prep wet wiping cloths for dinner service as they sit out for hours in ambient air growing bacteria in that time. COS- PIC removed wet cloths from carts.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-202.16: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. 

Rack holding server trays observed covered in duct tape that appears to be fraying. Cease practice of using duct tape as a covering on equipment in the kitchen as duct tape is prone to falling apart and not smooth and easily cleanable. Will follow up at next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

A number of new staff lack food handler cards. Discussed with PICs. Compile copies of food handler cards in public health binder for inspector to verify at next routine inspection. Handouts on online resources to complete training provided to PIC.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 (P) Food employee used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods. Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. 

Observed employee in kitchen chopping red cabbage without gloves on. Discussed with PIC and employee. Ensure staff are donning gloves when chopping RTE foods and produce.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

See #15. Freezer has created a layer of ice on most items within. Cardboard boxes that appear warped from ice or moisture should be discarded. Integrity of food packaging in both walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer should be intact to properly protect food. Most boxes appear in good condition (frozen fish from manufacturer), however noodle boxes appear warped. Noodles inside are packaged in plastic from the manufacturer. PIC asked to find a new container to store frozen noodles within. 

When preparing food to freeze ensure food is covered and packaged appropriately to prevent ice from accumulating on the food item itself.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed chopped produce being stored in the same cardboard boxes the whole produce had come in from food vendor. Discussed with PIC. When produce has been chopped and prepared, it must be transferred into a container that can be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Cardboard should not be reused in the kitchen, aside from catching grease at fryer station and changed out daily.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Walk-in freezer is completely iced over and there is significant ice accumulation on frozen foods prepared on baking sheets. Discussed contamination risk with PIC. As food thaws, any contamination from the ice/walls/ceilings will then drip onto food. Food must be protected from cross contamination via secure packaging and walk-ins should not accumulate ice. 

**All food stored on rolling racks in walk-in freezer, shrimp tempura stored on baking sheets, and any other food prepped and loosely wrapped in saran wrap on shelves voluntarily discarded by PIC at time of inspection. Food secured in cardboard boxes with integrity of box still in tact permitted to be kept at this time.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Cleavers stored on magnetic strip on wall above 3-compartment sink appear to be soiled with caked on food debris. Ensure knives and other utensils/equipment are sanitized and clean to sight and touch when not in use. Routinely wash, rinse sanitize magnetic strip as well to keep it suitable to store knives. Discussed with PIC, knives removed for cleaning.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process 

Observed raw shrimp thawing at room temperature at leaf of 3-compartment sink in kitchen. PIC stated an employee let it out to thaw while completing another task. Went over appropriate thawing practices with PIC. Food must be thawing under room temperature water in sink or thawing under refrigeration. Food may also thaw while being actively cooked. PIC moved shrimp into a pan of ice with running water. Within 15 minutes, employee had returned to further prepare shrimp. 
Ensure staff are aware of proper thawing practices with frozen product and complete the thawing and prep practice in a timely manner to limit time in ambient air.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14:  (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. 

Wet wiping cloths stored on hibachi cart in back stock area of kitchen. All wet cloths should be in an appropriate sanitizer solution. No wet wiping cloths out in ambient air. Ensure hibachi staff do not prep wet wiping cloths for dinner service as they sit out for hours in ambient air growing bacteria in that time.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The PERSON IN CHARGE shall:  (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;   (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ;(K) proper sanitizing;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD;

Inspector has visited facility on numerous occasions whether on complaint investigations, or on follow up's to routine inspections regarding food safety items pertaining to handwashing, handsink use, use of wiping cloths, and sanitizing. Despite extensive interaction with SCDPH officials, employees still fail to demonstrate proper food handling handwashing skills. Management does not appear to hold staff accountable to these standards and in turn, pose a risk to public health safety. SCDPH will contact facility and schedule additional training for staff at a later date.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. 

Observed employee at sushi bar using cell phone and then proceed to don gloves and continue prep of crab meat. Inspector intervened and asked employee to properly wash hands before putting on gloves. Employee then demonstrated a proper handwashing, including using a paper towel as a barrier. Inspector had just concluded a series of follow ups regarding handwashing at facility, it appears staff are aware of how to properly wash hands but fail to recognize interruptions in service where a handwash is needed. Discussed with PIC handwashing and role in potential FBI transmission.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only. 

See second #8 complaint. When inspector asked employee to wash hands, employee went to the second sink on the sushi station (next to wall) to attempt to wash hands. The designated handsink in the island is the center sink. Inspector asked employee to wash in the designated handsink. Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff are using only designated handsink to wash hands, and ensure handsinks are not used for other purposes.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: ( (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

Designated handsink in server station appears to be used as a dump sink as well (a discarded straw was observed lodged in the drain of the sink). Also observed a wet wiping rag stored within the handsink. Discussed with both front of house and back of house manager. If a sink is designated as a handsink, no other activity may occur there. Train waitstaff on which sinks may be used to dump drinks during service. Education provided. Rag removed.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P)

Various items are in the process of being prepped in the kitchen during inspection. Inspector observed a large bin of chopped carrots on the floor of kitchen. Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff are conscious of where they placed foods/utensils/equipment within restaurant. The items should be stored at least 6in off floor and in a place where it is not vulnerable to contamination. PIC moved carrots onto a table in kitchen.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14:  (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. 

Sanitizer rag at server station observed draped over bucket. Discussed with PIC. Ensure wet rags are properly stored within an acceptable sanitizer solution to prevent pathogen growth when exposed to open air conditions. Inspector placed rag completely submerged in bucket.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:  (D) In running water with sufficient velocity

Dipper well at sushi station is observed off at time of inspection. This is a repeat violation. If utensils are stored in the dipper well, the water must be flowing to rinse food debris away from in-use utensils. Inspector turned the dipper well back on.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.110: Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

Observed employee using cell phone during service behind the sushi bar. Ensure employees use designated spaces or break times to use the phone. Employees should not use phones in a food prep area due to the risk of contamination from phone, to hands, to food. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Observed sushi chef perform the following tasks while wearing the same pair of gloves/no hand wash or changes of gloves observed between tasks: Wheel cart for sushi rice to kitchen, scoop rice into container, place container in 3-part sink, use gloved hand to push on door to get back out to dining area, use a sanitizer rag to wipe down station, then proceed to make a sushi roll. 
Discussed with PIC. Staff continue to need proper training on washing hands and changing gloves between tasks, or when incidents occur that may have contaminated hands. Gloves are used for one task only, employees must not bounce from task to task while wearing the same gloves. PIC advised to work on training staff to recognize when a glove change is warranted and encourage staff to slow down, wash hands, and don new gloves during service.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

Hand sink in bar area observed to have the valve shut off during inspection. Hand sinks should be "on" at all times and plumbing should not be shut off under any circumstances, unless under maintenance. Cease practices of shutting off hand sinks when not in use. Inspector discussed with PIC and turned the valves under the sink to the "on" position.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Upon inspector arrival, a certified food manager was not present. Certified food manager arrived within 20 minutes of inspector arrival. A certified food manager must be present during all hours of operation. There should be enough certified managers on staff so that there is adequate coverage during hours of operation. Having a trained and certified manager on staff during operations is crucial to maintaining standards of food safety throughout service.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

See violation #15, ensure employees use a closed beverage container to prevent contamination via mouth or to prevent contamination due to an accidental spill.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed one employee complete a proper handwashing for 20 seconds with soap and hot water, then proceed to shut off the faucet with bare hands. Advised manager to host a training for all staff (most are new) on proper handwashing and ensure handwashing standards are maintained. Observed another employee do the same thing at a hand sink across the kitchen. Provided handouts to person in charge to assist in proper handwashing training.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only. 

Observed a staff member at the wok station use the faucet at the station to rinse hands then proceed to prepare food. This is an unacceptable practice because hands can only be washed in a handwashing station, where soil and debris can be washed away in a controlled space in the kitchen. Employees should not use other faucets/sinks for handwashing that are not designated because the splash, lack of soap, clean towels, etc. will risk contaminating surrounding utensils and equipment. Discussed with person in charge.

findings.comment:

Hand sink next to the dish machine did not have paper towels upon inspector arrival. Discussed with PIC. As soon as towels and/or soap are empty, employees must immediately replace the towels to ensure handwashing can be done during service. New paper towels were placed in the hand sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) \. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

Observed hand sink near the dish machine to have food debris clogging the drain. Also observed the server's hand sink to have cucumber slices within, which are used to garnish glasses of water. Discussed with PIC. When a sink is designated for handwashing, only handwashing may occur in this space. There should be no dumping of food or drink, no prepping, no rinsing of rags or utensils, etc. These practices pose a contamination risk to the establishment.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). 

Employee beverage (open glass container) stored in dry storage above dry goods on a lower shelf. Ensure staff do not store drinks, or any personal items in areas where customer food is either prepared or stored. Discussed with PIC. Drink was removed from the dry storage area and placed in the dish.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Hibachi service only occurs in evenings. Observed the hibachi carts stored in the kitchen area for dinner service tonight. The spatulas, tongs, forks present  in the hibachi cart were soiled with food and sauce debris, not clean and sanitized for service. Discussed with PIC. Ensure hibachi chefs keep their utensils and other equipment clean and sanitized to ensure they do not contaminate food during service. PIC removed the utensils, and the compartment they sat in, for cleaning.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. 

Throughout facility, wet wiping cloths are observed strewn about (kitchen, dish area, sushi bar, wait station). Discussed with PIC that soiled rags that are no longer in use must be removed and placed aside for washing and/or remain in a properly concentrated sanitizer solution. Wiping cloths were removed by PIC during inspection and placed aside for washing.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C)

Hibachi carts are stored in the kitchen for dinner service. On the lowest level of hibachi cart, wet wiping cloths are folded and stored for service. According to PIC, these cloths are utilized to wipe down the hibachi station equipment in between hibachi presentations. Cease practice of storing wet wiping cloths for service for indefinite amount of time. While sitting out, the rags will accumulate bacteria and other pathogens that may result in illness. Use a proper sanitizer bucket or ensure clean and sanitized equipment can be used at the start of each hibachi presentation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

There is an accumulation of debris in the following places: sides and lids of prep coolers, handles to fridges, sides of sushi bar display case, racks in dry storage, legs of shelving units and prep tables. Ensure periodic cleaning of sides/lids/handles of equipment are done to prevent general grease and soil accumulation. Discussed with PIC. Corrected.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. 

Per complaint, the ladies restroom hand sinks have very low pressure, a slow trickle. Inspector called a plumbing inspector to advise this aspect of inspection. A copy of the plumbing inspector's report was provided to food inspector and manager at Osaka to guide fixing the plumbing problem. Per plumbing inspector, PIC must have the plumbing repaired in 2 days by a licensed plumber. PIC advised to maintain a bill and/or invoice to verify service was completed appropriately. Follow up to occur in 2 business days.

findings.comment:

findings.comment:
